source_value.trigger: In state 4 the pointer is already on the inspector's Appearances popup; at 12.67s the popup menu opens over it showing 'None', a checked 'Any, Dark' and 'Any, Light, Dark', at 13.13s the blue highlight moves up from 'Any, Dark' to 'None', and by 13.93s the menu is gone and the Appearances row reads 'None'. No pressed state or click indicator is drawn, so the mouse-down itself cannot be read off the clip.
source_value.start_state: Xcode with the 'GratefulMoments' project open on its Assets catalog, the 'Ember' color set selected under Colors, two wells captioned 'Any Appearance' and 'Dark' under 'Universal' in the editor, and the inspector reading Name 'Ember', Devices 'Universal', Appearances 'Any, Dark', Gamut 'Any'. The toolbar reads 'GratefulMoments | iPhone 17 Pro' and the status field 'GratefulMoments: Ready | Today at 1:57 PM'.
source_value.end_state: The same window with Appearances reading 'None': the 'Dark' well and both well captions are gone and a single unlabelled well sits under 'Universal'. Nothing else changed, and from 14.07s to the 18.0s end no frame differs from its predecessor by more than 0.05/255.
source_value.continuity: Not one continuous take. At 15fps the clip cuts from the Xcode screen recording to a presenter shot at 2.40s (per-frame change 150.91/255) and cuts back to the same Xcode window at 7.13s (151.18/255); the intervening 4.7s show a person talking at a desk, not the product. Within each Xcode segment the frame never cuts and 214 of 269 frame pairs change by less than 0.2/255.
source_value.interruption_or_reversal: No interruption or reversal of the product change is shown: the popup opens once, the highlight moves once, and the committed 'None' value stays for the remaining 4.1s of the clip. The only thing that returns is the camera - the presenter cutaway at 2.40s ends at 7.13s on the same Xcode window, with the pointer in the same place.
source_value.feedback: The feedback is the menu itself: a check mark on the current value, a blue fill on the pointed row, and afterwards the editor silently dropping the second well. Mean per-frame change over the clip is 1.266/255, but that figure is dominated by the two cuts; the popup frames measure 0.299/255 at 12.67s, 0.442/255 at 13.13s and 0.217/255 at 13.73s. No progress indicator, badge, toast, undo affordance or confirmation text accompanies the change.
source_value.reduced_motion_equivalent: Both steps are single-frame hard changes - the menu appears in one frame at 12.67s and the value commits within the 13.73s-13.93s pair, with no fade, slide or easing frames measurable above 0.05/255 in between - so a still of state 4 and a still of state 5 carry the same information as the clip. Xcode's own Reduce Motion behaviour is not shown.
